XmlRpcTool.metaTitle: WordPress XML-RPC Checker - Scan xmlrpc Vulnerability
XmlRpcTool.metaDesc: Check if your WordPress site has xmlrpc.php enabled. Get detailed step-by-step instructions to disable it and prevent Brute Force & DDoS attacks.
XmlRpcTool.title: WordPress XML-RPC Checker
XmlRpcTool.desc: Check if your WordPress site has xmlrpc.php enabled. This file is often targeted by brute-force attacks and DDoS bots.
XmlRpcTool.cardDesc: Enter the URL of the WordPress site you want to scan.
XmlRpcTool.fixDesc: It is highly recommended to disable `xmlrpc.php` if you are not using it (e.g., for Jetpack or mobile app integration).
XmlRpcTool.seoDesc1: XML-RPC (XML Remote Procedure Call) is a protocol that allows external applications to communicate with WordPress via the xmlrpc.php file. In the past, it was used by the WordPress mobile app and services like Jetpack to post and manage content remotely.
XmlRpcTool.seoDesc2: However, since WordPress 4.7, the REST API has fully replaced XML-RPC, providing a much safer way to manage remote requests. The xmlrpc.php file is now a legacy feature that hackers actively scan for to find vulnerability backdoors.
XmlRpcTool.seoDesc3: According to Wordfence statistics, attacks targeting XML-RPC remain highly prevalent because hackers can leverage the multicall feature to test thousands of credentials in a single HTTP request, bypassing normal rate limits.
XmlRpcTool.attack1Desc: Uses XML-RPC's multicall feature to send thousands of login attempts in a single HTTP request. This easily bypasses standard rate limits and guesses passwords up to 100 times faster than normal login page attacks.
XmlRpcTool.attack2Desc: Attackers send pingback requests to your WordPress site to target another victim site. This forces your server to act as a proxy in DDoS amplification attacks, which can lead to high resource usage and IP blacklisting.
XmlRpcTool.attack3Desc: Even failed login attempts generate significant CPU and server load because WordPress still has to load and parse each XML request. This can crash or severely slow down your website.
XmlRpcTool.seoProtectDesc: There are multiple ways to block or restrict access to xmlrpc.php. Choose the method that best matches your hosting setup and website needs.
XmlRpcTool.protect1Desc: Blocks requests at the web server level before WordPress loads. Maximum resource saving. Ideal for shared hosting.
XmlRpcTool.protect2Desc: Disables XML-RPC via WordPress filters. Easy and safe, but WordPress still loads first. Good if you cannot edit server configs.
XmlRpcTool.protect3Desc: Add a location block in nginx.conf to return a 403 Forbidden. Efficient server-level blocking. Ideal for VPS/Cloud.
XmlRpcTool.faq1Q: What is XML-RPC and how does it work on WordPress?
XmlRpcTool.faq1A: XML-RPC is a remote procedural call protocol using XML to encode its calls and HTTP as a transport mechanism. It is deprecated and largely replaced by the REST API, making it an unnecessary security risk.
XmlRpcTool.faq2A: Its multicall feature allows attackers to bundle thousands of username/password combinations into a single request, speeding up brute force attacks and enabling pingback DDoS amplification.
XmlRpcTool.faq3Q: Will disabling XML-RPC break my site?
XmlRpcTool.faq3A: Only if you use Jetpack, the WooCommerce mobile app, or other plugins that rely on XML-RPC. For standard websites, disabling it has no impact and significantly improves security.
XmlRpcTool.faq4Q: What is the best way to disable XML-RPC?
XmlRpcTool.faq4A: Blocking it at the server level via .htaccess (for Apache) or nginx.conf (for Nginx) is the most efficient and recommended way to save resources.
XmlRpcTool.faq5A: Yes, plugins like Wordfence and iThemes Security have built-in options to block XML-RPC, but server-level blocking remains the most efficient shield.

ApiTester.metaTitle: Online API Tester - Test REST API GET/POST
ApiTester.metaDesc: Test REST API requests instantly from your browser without installing Postman. Supports importing from cURL, fetch, Axios, Python requests, Go net/http with response viewer and request history.
ApiTester.metaKeywords: API Tester, REST API tester, test API online, cURL import, Postman alternative, API debugging, HTTP client online, test REST API
ApiTester.faq1Q: How does this API Tester differ from Postman?
ApiTester.faq1A: This API Tester runs directly in your browser without requiring any software installation, making it ideal for quick tests or when using devices where software installation is restricted. Postman offers a more complete set of features for enterprise use, such as collections, environment variables, and automated testing.
ApiTester.faq2Q: Why is a proxy required to send requests?
ApiTester.faq2A: Browsers enforce a CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) policy that prevents calling APIs from other domains directly. Our proxy acts as an intermediary, sending the request on behalf of the browser to resolve this issue, without storing any logs or your data.
ApiTester.faq3Q: What coding languages are supported for importing?
ApiTester.faq3A: It supports 7 formats: Bash cURL, PHP cURL, JavaScript fetch, Axios, Python requests, HTTPie, and Go net/http. Simply paste the code into the Import box and click Extract. The system will automatically retrieve the URL, method, headers, and body to fill in the form.
ApiTester.faq4Q: Where is the API request history stored?
ApiTester.faq4A: All history is saved locally in your browser's localStorage. No data is sent to any servers, meaning that if you switch browsers or clear your browser data, your history will be lost.
ApiTester.faq5Q: Can this be used to test APIs that require Authentication?
ApiTester.faq5A: Yes, you can add headers in the Headers section (JSON format), such as {"Authorization": "Bearer your-token"} or {"X-API-Key": "your-key"}. The system will send those headers with every request.
ApiTester.methodGetDesc: Retrieves data from the server without making modifications. Ideal for loading lists or resource details.
ApiTester.methodPostDesc: Creates new data on the server by sending a body with the request. Used for login, creating new records.
ApiTester.methodPutDesc: Replaces all data of the specified resource. Must send all fields.
ApiTester.methodPatchDesc: Updates parts of the resource data. Sends only the fields that need modification.
ApiTester.methodDeleteDesc: Deletes the specified resource from the server. Warning: This action is usually irreversible.

ApiTester.whatIsApiTesterHeader: What is an Online API Tester?
ApiTester.whatIsApiTesterDesc1: An API Tester is a tool for testing connections and verifying the functionality of a REST API without writing code or installing additional software. Developers use these tools to send HTTP requests to various endpoints and inspect the responses received, including status codes, headers, or bodies.
ApiTester.whatIsApiTesterDesc2: This tool supports automatic code import from 7 formats, including Bash cURL, PHP cURL, JavaScript fetch, Axios, Python requests, HTTPie, and Go net/http, allowing you to paste and test code generated from AI or API documentation instantly without manual conversion.
ApiTester.whatIsApiTesterDesc3: All requests are routed through a Cloudflare Worker Proxy to resolve CORS issues where browsers block cross-domain API calls directly. All request history is recorded solely in your localStorage, and no logs are saved on any servers.
ApiTester.step1Desc: Paste cURL/fetch/Axios code into the Import box and click Extract, or enter the URL and select the HTTP method directly. Include Headers and Body as needed.
ApiTester.step2Desc: Click the Send Request button to fire the API. The system routes it through the Proxy automatically to bypass CORS and displays results in real-time.
ApiTester.step3Desc: View status codes, response times, body (JSON formatted), and headers in separate tabs. The request history is saved automatically for reuse.
ApiTester.privacySecurityDesc: The proxy used for sending requests runs on Cloudflare Workers, an edge runtime that does not log connections or payloads. It only forwards requests and returns responses. All request history is saved strictly in your browser's localStorage and can be deleted at any time using the 'Clear All' button.

BackgroundRemover.metaDesc: Remove background from JPG, PNG, and WebP images to transparent PNG or WebP at full resolution. Uses local WebGPU by default, with Cloudflare fallback and Turnstile when needed.
BackgroundRemover.metaKeywords: remove background, remove image background, background remover online, AI background remover, transparent PNG, transparent WebP, cutout background, local-first AI, WebGPU AI, Cloudflare Turnstile
BackgroundRemover.ogTitle: Remove Image Background Online - AI Background Remover
BackgroundRemover.ogDesc: Extract objects from backgrounds using local-first AI. Export transparent PNG/WebP, with Cloudflare fallback and Turnstile when WebGPU is unavailable.
BackgroundRemover.twitterTitle: Remove Image Background Online - AI Background Remover
BackgroundRemover.twitterDesc: Remove background from JPG, PNG, WebP to transparent file at full resolution. Uses local WebGPU, with Cloudflare fallback when needed.
BackgroundRemover.faq1Q: Is it safe to remove image backgrounds with this tool?
BackgroundRemover.faq1A: Absolutely. The system runs local-first by default, meaning your images are processed within your device's browser and never sent to any server (when using WebGPU AI or Canvas Heuristics). If you choose Cloudflare AI Fallback, the image is sent securely to Cloudflare's server for processing and is never permanently stored on their servers.
BackgroundRemover.faq2Q: Why does the first run take longer to process?
BackgroundRemover.faq2A: When using WebGPU AI for the first time, the system needs to download the image processing AI model (BiRefNet-lite) from Hugging Face. The model size is about 114MB for devices supporting float16, or about 224MB for float32. This download happens only once. The model is then stored in your browser cache, making subsequent uses instant without reloading.
BackgroundRemover.faq3Q: What if my device or browser does not support WebGPU?
BackgroundRemover.faq3A: No problem. The system is designed with backup engines. It automatically detects and switches to Canvas Heuristics to quickly remove solid color backgrounds. Alternatively, you can choose Cloudflare AI Fallback for complex images, which requires Turnstile verification to prevent abuse.
BackgroundRemover.faq4Q: What is the format of the output image?
BackgroundRemover.faq4A: Once the background is removed, you can download the result either as a transparent PNG (maintaining 100% of the original resolution, perfect for further editing) or as a transparent WebP (compressed for a much smaller file size while keeping high quality, perfect for websites or social media).
BackgroundRemover.faq5Q: How is the Cloudflare AI Fallback quota managed?
BackgroundRemover.faq5A: To save upload bandwidth and resources, the system calls the Cloudflare API only once per image to retrieve the transparent PNG. The conversion to WebP then occurs locally in your browser. The Cloudflare fallback button for that image is disabled immediately after a successful run to prevent redundant requests.
BackgroundRemover.faq6Q: What are the recommended image dimensions and file sizes?
BackgroundRemover.faq6A: Our tool supports images up to 32 megapixels. However, for optimal performance and to avoid Out of Memory (OOM) errors in your browser when running AI on your GPU, we recommend using images under 15-20MB.
BackgroundRemover.faq7Q: Can I use the background remover offline?
BackgroundRemover.faq7A: Yes! Once the AI model (WebGPU) has been successfully downloaded on your device, it is kept in Cache Storage. You can then drop images and remove backgrounds 100% offline without any internet connection.
BackgroundRemover.faq8Q: How do I remove the AI model from my device?
BackgroundRemover.faq8A: If you are concerned about storage space and want to remove the model, you can do so easily by clearing your browser cache for yuukub.com, or open Developer Tools, go to Application -> Storage, and click 'Clear site data'.

BackgroundRemover.whyLocalTitle: Why Should You Remove Backgrounds Local-first?
BackgroundRemover.whyLocal1Desc: Most background removal sites require uploading your files to their servers. Our local-first system runs Transformers.js with WebGPU directly in your browser. Your portrait, product photos, or documents never leave your device.
BackgroundRemover.whyLocal2Desc: Cloud AI has high server costs, so services often restrict usage or downscale images to low resolution. Since our tool uses your device's GPU/CPU power, you can remove backgrounds and download high-resolution images infinitely.
BackgroundRemover.whyLocal3Desc: For WebGPU, the AI model (BiRefNet-lite) is downloaded once to your browser cache. Subsequent runs load the model instantly offline, saving megabytes of cellular data.
BackgroundRemover.whyLocal4Desc: If your device lacks a GPU or runs an old browser, the tool falls back to Canvas Heuristics for solid backgrounds, or you can verify via Turnstile to use Cloudflare Workers AI Fallback.

faq.q1: Is converting images with this tool safe?
faq.a1: 100% safe because all files are processed locally via WebAssembly inside your browser. No files are sent to any server. Your private images or confidential documents will never be leaked.
faq.q2: How large of a file is supported?
faq.a2: It depends on your device's RAM. Generally, it supports files up to tens of MBs per file, and you can convert multiple files at once without limit. We recommend converting 10–20 files at a time for optimal performance.
faq.q3: Why is WebP better than JPEG for websites?
faq.a3: WebP offers similar quality but is 25–34% smaller on average compared to JPEG. This makes pages load faster, reduces bandwidth usage, and improves Core Web Vitals (LCP), which directly benefits SEO. It is supported by all modern browsers.
faq.q4: What is the difference between AVIF and WebP?
faq.a4: AVIF is a newer format that compresses 20–50% better than WebP, but it takes longer to encode. It is suitable for websites needing maximum performance. WebP remains a great choice if you prioritize conversion speed and wider browser support.
faq.q5: Can I convert an image back to its original format to re-compress it?
faq.a5: Yes. This tool supports PNG → PNG or WebP → WebP conversion to re-compress files using your preferred Quality setting, which is very useful for reducing file sizes without changing formats.

webp.desc: Suitable for all types of images on websites. Provides file sizes up to 30% smaller than JPEG with almost no quality difference. Helps pages load faster and improves SEO. Supported by all modern browsers.

avif.title: High-Performance Websites
avif.desc: Ideal for websites requiring high Core Web Vitals scores, such as e-commerce or landing pages where every millisecond counts. Offers the best compression, but encodes slower than WebP.

png.title: Graphics and Logos
png.desc: Best for images requiring a transparent background (transparency) like logos, icons, and UI elements. Delivers maximum lossless quality, but file sizes are larger than other formats.

jpeg.title: Photos and Legacy CMS
jpeg.desc: Perfect for photos that need to be uploaded to legacy CMS systems or platforms that only support JPG. Supported by all devices and browsers, making it the safest option for compatibility.

whyImportant.title: Why is Image Conversion Important?
whyImportant.p1: In an era where website speed directly impacts user experience and SEO rankings, choosing the right image format is something developers and website owners should not overlook. Images are often the largest files on a webpage, and choosing the wrong format can significantly slow down your site.
whyImportant.p2: Modern formats like WebP and AVIF are designed to solve this directly, reducing file sizes by 25–50% compared to traditional JPEG or PNG without noticeable quality loss. This improves Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), one of the Core Web Vitals Google uses for rankings.
whyImportant.p3: Additionally, sometimes format conversion is necessary for system compatibility, such as CMS platforms that only support JPEG or PNG. Or when you need images with transparent backgrounds, you must use PNG, WebP, or AVIF instead of JPEG, which does not support this feature.

compare.title: Comparison: JPEG vs PNG vs WebP vs AVIF
compare.footer: The table above provides an overview of each format. When choosing a format, consider file size, transparency requirements, and your target audience's browser compatibility. Generally, WebP is the most balanced choice for websites today.

faqItems.question: Are uploaded PDF files safe?
faqItems.answer: 100% safe because all files are processed solely within your browser. No files are uploaded to any server, making this ideal for confidential documents or personal information.

faqItems.question: How large a PDF file is supported?
faqItems.answer: It depends on your device's RAM. Generally, files up to several tens of MB are supported for Merge and Split. For PDF→JPG, processing may take longer if the PDF has dozens of pages. We recommend handling no more than 50 pages at a time for optimal performance.

faqItems.question: What resolution do I get for PDF→JPG?
faqItems.answer: The system renders pages at 2x scale (192 DPI) for crisp images suitable for web use or presentations. You can adjust the JPG quality from 50 to 100 to balance file size and quality.

faqItems.question: Are password-protected PDFs supported?
faqItems.answer: No, encrypted or password-protected PDFs cannot be processed. Please remove the password protection before using the tool.

faqItems.question: Can I arrange files before merging?
faqItems.answer: Yes, in Merge mode, each file displays a thumbnail of the first page with left/right arrows ◀▶ to adjust their order. For page-level adjustments, use the 'Organize PDF' tab, which supports dragging and dropping thumbnails for every page.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between 'Merge PDF' and 'Organize PDF'?
faqItems.answer: Merge PDF is used to join multiple PDF files together in a sequence. Organize PDF offers more flexibility, allowing you to drag and drop individual pages, delete unwanted pages, and mix pages from different PDFs in a custom sequence.

faqItems.question: How much can PDF size be reduced and what are the results?
faqItems.answer: It depends on the content and mode: Rasterize (converting pages to JPEG images) reduces size by 50–90%, ideal for scanned or image-heavy docs (but text becomes non-selectable). Smart Mode (object stream compression) preserves selectable text but reduces size by only 1–10%. For major size reduction, use Rasterize.
